#### 1. combined immunodeficiency due to STIM1 deficiency  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.789)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-983695, Reactome:R-HSA-139853, Reactome:R-HSA-5578775)

**Proposed mechanism:** STIM1 (HGNC:11386) —DISRUPTS→ Calcium influx and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) (GO:0005810); Calcium influx and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) (GO:0005810) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001894); Calcium influx and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) (GO:0005810) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002777); Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002777) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent infections (HP:0011073). Loss-of-function mutations in STIM1 disrupt calcium influx and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE). This disruption leads to defective platelet function, resulting in thrombocytopenia (Stormorken syndrome), and impaired T-cell and B-cell function, causing combined immunodeficiency and recurrent infections.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of patients with Stormorken syndrome carrying STIM1 mutations predicted to cause gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, or the identification of patients with combined immunodeficiency due to STIM1 deficiency with mutations that do not impair calcium influx, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing a high frequency (>1%) of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in STIM1 in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of STIM1 in both platelet function and immune cell signaling can inform the development of targeted therapies for patients with these rare disorders, potentially addressing both bleeding risks and susceptibility to infections.
